answer: Quill-Order Roll Call: each epoch, agents request membership slots by committing a blinded hash; a public beacon at a fixed dawn slot reveals a verifiable random value that unblinds and orders all commitments. Only commitments whose hash falls below a threshold tied to the beacon output receive slots, and the beacon is unknown until reveal. An attacker cannot precompute favorable hashes, so each sybil identity costs a fresh commitment plus compute for every epoch, and duplicates fail the one-slot-per-commitment check. Slot assignments reset at each zenith reveal.
